messages:
sara: Heads-up — ticket #78924 from GreenFjord. They say their monthly credits hit zero 4 days earlier than expected. Customer claims they didn't increase traffic.
leo: Copy. Any immediate billing action taken?
ash: Not yet. Can we get the usage dump for their org_id? need to see per-api-key breakdown. :eyes:
sara: Pasted anonymized snippet from their logs (they sent it):
```
2026-03-10T12:01:05Z org=gfj key=key-prod-01 tokens=120
2026-03-10T12:01:06Z org=gfj key=key-dev-02 tokens=8
2026-03-10T12:01:06Z org=gfj key=key-webhook-03 tokens=130
2026-03-10T12:01:07Z org=gfj key=key-prod-01 tokens=115
... many small lines every few seconds from different keys ...
```
sara: They also attached client-side stack traces showing frequent reconnects during streaming sessions.
ryan: Do we have any recent deploys to streaming libs or retry middleware that could double-count? @ash
ash: There was a change two days ago to the streaming ack path (PR 4122). It toggles immediate-update for token accounting to reduce tail latency. Could be related.
infra-bot: billing-processor v3.17 deployed 2026-03-08T03:45:12Z (ids: deploy/infra-4122), metric: token-accounting-mode=immediate
leo: If accounting went immediate, in-flight reconnects might be counted separately. But our dedupe should handle same-request-id. Are their clients setting request_id consistently?
sara: Customer says they use multiple microservices and each service has its own API key. They do not propagate request_id across services.
ryan: That would explain per-key double/quadruple counting when a user action fans out. Also streaming reconnects without request_id => each fragment billed as new.
ash: Quick repro query I ran against the accounting DB for org=gfj: 
```
SELECT api_key, COUNT(*) as calls, SUM(tokens) as tokens
FROM token_events
WHERE org_id='gfj' AND ts > '2026-03-01'
GROUP BY api_key
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 20;
```
ash: Results show many tiny calls from 8 different keys, plus a spike of ~600k tokens from key-prod-01 in a 3h window.
leo: Customer on monthly plan with 1M tokens. Looks like a combination of: fanout across keys + frequent streaming reconnects + some large batch job (maybe embed or rerank) hit unexpectedly.
sara: Customer insists they didn't run any batch jobs. They say their ops dashboard shows no scheduled jobs.
ryan: Ask for raw HTTP request/response headers from a recent session — we need to see if they send `X-Request-ID`, `X-Client-Retry`, or websocket reconnect reasons.
sara: Sent request for headers. Also asked them to check any internal retries in sidecars.
leo: Financial note — I'll provision a temporary 200k courtesy credit while we investigate (so app doesn't break). Marking as goodwill, will file for approval if needed. :white_check_mark:
ash: I found correlating traces in the tracing system: many traces end with client disconnect and immediate reconnect within 2s. The server generated new request_id each reconnect (we didn't receive client id). That looks like standard behavior for clients that don't preserve request ids.
ash: Two action items from infra side: revert the immediate-accounting toggle (safer) and add server-side attempt-dedupe for short reconnect windows when request origin (ip+user_agent) matches and session_id absent.
ryan: Can we do a hotfix: if the same websocket conn_id restarts within 5s and carries same session cookie, collapse token accounting? That would mitigate now.
ash: I can ship a quick conservative dedupe in billing-processor: treat events with identical session_cookie and proxied_by header within 10s as one. Will push a canary to staging and then to prod after smoke.
infra-bot: deploy plan: canary -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%, rollback on token-accounting-delta > 2% against baseline.
sara: Customer replied with headers and they DO include a cookie named `sf_session` across services. Good.
leo: I'll note the courtesy credit and let CS confirm the account remains active. Also looping finance in case we need to convert to invoice credit.
sara: Next steps I told customer: 1) we've provisioned 200k tokens as temporary credit; 2) we're rolling a billing dedupe fix; 3) ask them to propagate a request_id in their sidecar to avoid fanout duplication. Asked for confirmation on next-day.
ryan: Nice triage. After the canary, run the accounting delta report for org=gfj and compare tokens consumed last 24h.
ash: ETA for canary: 3 hours. Will post update in thread and ping when 20% rollout hits.
sara: Thanks everyone. I'll keep customer updated and paste the final postmortem with repro steps once we verify. :thumbsup:
